info.title: CoderPad Screen API community contract
info.description: Community-maintained Screen v1.1 contract. Authenticate requests using the API-Key header. Additive response fields can appear without a version change; consumers should preserve unknown JSON where appropriate.

post.description: Stores a file and returns the id to reference it with in a later call. The file is the raw request body and must not exceed 52428800 bytes (50 MB). Its 'Content-Length' header is optional, but when it is set it must be the exact byte size of the body: a length smaller than the body stores a truncated file. Uploading requires the same permission as saving a question, which is the only call an upload can be referenced by. An upload no later call has referenced is eventually deleted, so it should be referenced promptly.

post.description:
You can create a webhook or contact us to do so.

Only one webhook can be configured at a time. A new subscription will replace the existing one.

Every time an event is triggered on the platform, this webhook is updated with the event type and any necessary details.

Here are the events currently sent to this webhook:

 - "test_status_changed": when a test status changes (completed, canceled, ?)

SaveQuestionRequest.description: Question data to create or update. Same structure as QuestionDetailsResult without the server-owned fields. An unknown property is rejected, so a fetched question cannot be sent back as is: its read-only fields must be stripped first. Top level: 'id', 'version', 'creation_time', 'modification_time', 'from_coderpad_question_bank', 'resources', 'game_details' and 'file_upload_details'. Nested: 'code_details.available_programming_language_ids' and 'project_details.download_url'. 'evaluation.test_report' is read-only too, but it is declared here, so it is refused as a block the question type does not support rather than as an unknown property

ArrayNode.description: An evolving JSON item emitted by AI Assist.

creation_time.description: creation date of the conversation (ISO 8601, UTC)

messages.description: the messages of the conversation, oldest first

ai_assist_conversation.description: a conversation between the candidate and the AI assistant

conversations.description: the conversations, oldest first. Empty when the candidate did not use the AI assistant

ai_assist_conversations.description: the conversations the candidate had with the AI assistant on a PROJECT question

role.description: USER for a message of the candidate, ASSISTANT for an answer of the AI

creation_time.description: creation date of the message (ISO 8601, UTC)

output_items.description: the parts of the message, in the format the AI assistant stores them, which may evolve. Each item has an id, a type, a status and its startedAt / finishedAt times in milliseconds. A message item carries its text chunks in content, a reasoning item the summary of the AI reasoning, and a function_call, web_search or code_execution item what the AI asked for (name and arguments, or queries), never its result.

ai_assist_message.description: a message of an AI assist conversation

value.description: the accepted answer, as an exact value or a regular expression

match_type.description: how the candidate answer is compared with this accepted answer: EXACT is a case insensitive, trimmed equality, REGEX a full match of the whole answer. Same values as the question API publishes

accepted_answer.description: an answer the question accepts as correct, the candidate answer is matched against each of them

rationale.description: the message explaining the AI recommendation

recommended_outcome.description: the verdict the AI recommends on this criterion, stated the same way as outcome so a caller never has to translate one into the other. Only ever PASSED or FAILED: the AI reaching no recommendation is reported by omitting this field, see no_recommendation_reason

no_recommendation_reason.description: why the AI produced no recommendation for this criterion. Omitted when it did. This never describes the candidate's result, only the AI review

ai_review.description: AI assisted review of a rubric criterion

answer.description: the answer of the candidate, in the {type}_answer sub-block of the question type

label.description: the choice label, in the language the candidate took the test in

choice.description: a single choice of an MCQ question

correct_choice_indexes.description: zero based positions of the correct choices in mcq_details.choices, to compare with answer.mcq_answer.selected_choice_indexes. Same positions as the correct_choice_indexes of GET /v1.1/questions/{id}

items.description: zero based positions of the correct choices in mcq_details.choices, to compare with answer.mcq_answer.selected_choice_indexes. Same positions as the correct_choice_indexes of GET /v1.1/questions/{id}

choice_selection.description: the choices the candidate had to select

code.description: the code of the candidate's last submission

programming_language_id.description: id of the programming language chosen by the candidate. Omitted on a question available in a single language, since the question imposes it

code_answer.description: what the candidate submitted on a CODE question

url.description: url to the test report through the dashboard application

send_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) when the test has been sent

start_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) when the test has been started

end_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) when the test has been ended

candidate_language.description: the language chosen by the candidate to take the test if they started the test, null otherwise

last_activity_time.description: time (in milliseconds) of the candidate's last activity (last submit or code test)

approval_status.description: approval status of the candidate (PASSED, REJECTED, TO_REVIEW)

timer_type.description: how the test times the candidate. PER_QUESTION is the only mode where a question has a limit of its own, so it is the only one where a question carries a time_limit_seconds: a GLOBAL test times the whole session and an UNLIMITED one times nothing. Omitted on a test the candidate never started

questions.description: the questions of the test with their detailed report data. Omitted when the caller is not allowed to access detailed reports

evaluation.description: how the candidate answer was graded, and the result of each grading criterion

filename.description: name of the file uploaded by the candidate

download_url.description: signed download url of the file uploaded by the candidate. This url is temporary and expires, do not store it

candidate_comment.description: comment left by the candidate along with the file

file_upload_answer.description: what the candidate uploaded on a FILE_UPLOAD question

code.description: the code of the candidate's last submission

programming_language_id.description: id of the programming language chosen by the candidate. Omitted on a question available in a single language, since the question imposes it

game_answer.description: what the candidate submitted on a GAME question

test_cases.description: test cases of the question, each with its result. A question nesting its validators returns the whole tree flattened, a parent before its own children, so the max_points of the list add up to the question max_points

input_output.description: result of the test cases comparing the output of the candidate code with the expected one

skill.description: skill assessed by this test case

outcome.description: verdict of the test case. NOT_RUN when it was never run, typically because the candidate never submitted or a previous test case timed out: an unrun test case is undecided, never failed. PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW never applies here, only a rubric criterion waits for a human

max_points.description: points the test case is worth, the points of the question API

awarded_points.description: points the candidate obtained on this test case, null while it has not been decided

result_message.description: explains the result of this test case: the test runner output, or the reason it was not run. Free text meant to be displayed, not parsed

result_overridden_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter set this result by hand instead of leaving it to the automatic grading. A CoderPad admin or a write-access shared report can do it too, never CoderPad itself. outcome and awarded_points already reflect it, so a caller never applies it itself

timed_out.description: whether the test case timed out

input_output_test_case.description: result of one test case comparing the output of the candidate code with the expected one

selected_choice_indexes.description: zero based positions of the choices the candidate picked, in mcq_details.choices

items.description: zero based positions of the choices the candidate picked, in mcq_details.choices

mcq_answer.description: what the candidate picked on an MCQ question

choices.description: every choice of the question, listed in the question's own order. A choice is pointed at by its position in this list, the way GET /v1.1/questions/{id} does, by correct_choice_indexes and by answer.mcq_answer.selected_choice_indexes

selection_mode.description: whether the candidate can select one or multiple choices: SINGLE or MULTIPLE

mcq_details.description: MCQ specific configuration of the question

download_url.description: url of the endpoint building the candidate project archive (question project with the candidate changes applied). It requires the API-Key header and generates the archive on demand, so expect a slow response. Only returned when the candidate submitted the project at least once.

ai_assist_conversation_count.description: number of conversations the candidate had with the AI assistant on this question. Fetch them from GET /tests/{id}/questions/{questionId}/ai-assist-conversations.

project_answer.description: what the candidate submitted on a PROJECT question

url.description: signed url of the recording. This url is temporary and expires, do not store it. Only returned when video_details.recording_availability is AVAILABLE

transcript_url.description: signed url of the recording transcript. This url is temporary and expires. Returned whenever the transcript file still exists, even when the recording itself is gone: anonymisation deletes the media and keeps the transcript, while the candidate's own deletion removes both

duration_seconds.description: length (in seconds) of the recording, not a time the candidate spent

recording.description: a single recording of a VIDEO answer

duration.description: duration (in seconds) spent by the candidate to complete the test

points.description: number of points awarded to the test

total_duration.description: maximal duration (in seconds) available for the test

comparative_score.description: candidate score compared with developers who have taken a similar test

marked_as_cheated_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter manually flagged this candidate as cheated. Never set by CoderPad: the platform own detections are reported as warnings instead. The question level flag is questions[].marked_as_cheated_by_recruiter

time_spent_outside_environment_seconds.description: total time (in seconds) the candidate spent with the environment out of focus during the test

environment_exit_count.description: number of times the candidate left the environment during the test

points.description: number of points awarded to the test for the given technology and the specific skill

score.description: number of points in percentage for the given technology and the specific skill

total_points.description: available points for the test for the given technology and the specific skill

report_skill.description: report by skill for a given technology - the property name is the skill name, 'Language Knowledge' or 'Problem Solving' for instance

points.description: number of points awarded to the test for the given technology

score.description: number of points in percentage for the given technology

total_points.description: available points for the test for the given technology

comparative_score.description: candidate score compared with developers who have taken a similar test for the given technology

report_technology.description: report by technology - the property name is the technology name, 'PHP' for instance

criteria.description: criteria of the rubric, in the order the question defines them, each with the result of its review

rubric.description: result of the review of the answer against the question rubric

description.description: reviewer-facing description of what the criterion expects

outcome.description: verdict of the criterion. PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW while a human still has to grade it, which puts the whole question in PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW too. NOT_RUN when nobody is expected to grade it, typically because the candidate never answered the question. An AI_GRADING criterion is graded by the AI, so it is decided without ever being PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW

max_points.description: points the criterion is worth, the points of the question API

awarded_points.description: points the reviewer awarded, null while the criterion has not been reviewed

result_message.description: explains the result of this criterion. Free text meant to be displayed, not parsed. Only on a question whose criteria are validators the platform records a message for, such as a FILE_UPLOAD

result_overridden_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter set this result by hand instead of leaving it to the grading. A CoderPad admin or a write-access shared report can do it too, never CoderPad itself. outcome and awarded_points already reflect it, so a caller never applies it itself

review_mode.description: how the criterion is reviewed, the review_mode of the question API

rubric_criterion.description: result of one criterion of the rubric the answer was reviewed against

outcome.description: verdict of the comparison. NOT_RUN when it was never run, typically because the candidate never submitted: an unrun comparison is undecided, never failed

max_points.description: points the comparison is worth, which is the whole question

awarded_points.description: points the candidate obtained, null while the comparison has not been decided

result_message.description: explains the result of the comparison. Free text meant to be displayed, not parsed

result_overridden_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter set this result by hand instead of leaving it to the automatic grading. A CoderPad admin or a write-access shared report can do it too, never CoderPad itself. outcome and awarded_points already reflect it, so a caller never applies it itself

sql_query_result_comparison.description: result of comparing the candidate query result with the reference one

id.description: the question global id, stable across versions. Same id as GET /v1.1/questions/{id}

version.description: the version of the question the candidate answered

type.description: the question type, with the same values as the question API publishes

warnings.description: warnings raised on this question. report.warnings holds the test session ones, so a warning is here or there, never in both

awarded_points.description: points the candidate obtained on this question. A question waiting for its review reports the points already awarded, 0 when none is. Omitted while the test is not finished, and on a campaign hiding the scores from the recruiters, where max_points is omitted too

time_limit_seconds.description: time limit (in seconds) of the question. Only returned when the test timer_type is PER_QUESTION, the only mode where a question has a limit of its own

time_spent_seconds.description: time (in seconds) the candidate actually spent on this question, whatever the timer_type. Can exceed time_limit_seconds when the timer was tampered with

first_access_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) of the first time the candidate opened the question

submission_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) at which the candidate submitted this question, the last submission when there are several. Absent when the candidate never submitted it. A save or a code test does not move it, last_activity_time does

last_activity_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) of the candidate's last activity on this question (last submit or code test)

answer_status.description: what the candidate produced on this question, whatever its type. Resolved in that order: NOT_STARTED (no first_access_time), NOT_SUBMITTED (no submission_time), EMPTY (submitted nothing at all), STARTER_CODE_UNCHANGED (submitted the starter untouched, CODE, GAME and PROJECT only), ANSWERED otherwise. Returned while the test is still running as well, unlike the other candidate fields: it says where the candidate stands, not how they did, and it can still change until the test ends

grading_status.description: how far the grading of the question went, so a caller knows whether awarded_points can still change. GRADED when every criterion that could be decided was, PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW while a human still has to grade one of them, NOT_GRADED when none was ever decided, typically an unanswered question. It is not a verdict: awarded_points against max_points and the outcome of each criterion carry the result itself

timed_out.description: whether the candidate ran out of time on this question

result_overridden_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter set the result of this question by hand instead of leaving it to the automatic grading. A CoderPad admin or a write-access shared report can do it too, never CoderPad itself. awarded_points already reflects it, so a caller never applies it itself. Each test case carries the same flag for its own result

marked_as_cheated_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter manually flagged this answer as cheated. Never set by CoderPad: the platform own detections are reported as warnings instead. The candidate level flag is report.marked_as_cheated_by_recruiter

time_spent_outside_environment_seconds.description: total time (in seconds) the candidate spent with the environment out of focus during this question

environment_exit_count.description: number of times the candidate left the environment during this question

test_question.description: detailed report data of a single question of the test

test_cases.description: tests of the suite, in the order the question defines them, each with its result

test_report.description: result of the project test suite run on the candidate answer

key.description: stable identifier of the test case, the key of the question API

label.example: Returns the first page by default

skill.description: skill assessed by this test case

outcome.description: verdict of the test case. NOT_RUN when the suite never ran it, typically because the candidate never submitted: an unrun test case is undecided, never failed. PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW never applies here, only a rubric criterion waits for a human

output.description: raw output produced by the test run

test_identifier.description: identifier of the test in the project test suite

max_points.description: points the test case is worth, the points of the question API

awarded_points.description: points the candidate obtained on this test case, null while it has not been decided

result_overridden_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter set this result by hand instead of leaving it to the test suite. A CoderPad admin or a write-access shared report can do it too, never CoderPad itself. outcome and awarded_points already reflect it, so a caller never applies it itself

test_report_test_case.description: result of one test of the project test suite

text.description: the free text answer written by the candidate

text_answer.description: what the candidate wrote on a TEXT question

accepted_answers.description: the answers the question accepts, the candidate answer being matched against each of them. They carry no verdict of their own: the platform stops at the first match, so only the question level grading_status and awarded_points say whether the answer was accepted

text_answer_matching.description: how the candidate text was matched against the answers the question accepts

test_cases.description: test cases of the question, each with its result. A question nesting its validators returns the whole tree flattened, a parent before its own children, so the max_points of the list add up to the question max_points

validation_code.description: result of the validation methods run against the candidate code

label.example: Evicts the least recently used entry

skill.description: skill assessed by this test case

outcome.description: verdict of the test case. NOT_RUN when it was never run, typically because the candidate never submitted or a previous test case timed out: an unrun test case is undecided, never failed. PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW never applies here, only a rubric criterion waits for a human

test_identifier.description: name of the validation method running the test case

max_points.description: points the test case is worth, the points of the question API

awarded_points.description: points the candidate obtained on this test case, null while it has not been decided

result_message.description: explains the result of this test case: the test runner output, or the reason it was not run. Free text meant to be displayed, not parsed

result_overridden_by_recruiter.description: whether a recruiter set this result by hand instead of leaving it to the automatic grading. A CoderPad admin or a write-access shared report can do it too, never CoderPad itself. outcome and awarded_points already reflect it, so a caller never applies it itself

timed_out.description: whether the test case timed out

validation_code_test_case.description: result of one validation method run against the candidate code

recordings.description: the recordings of the answer, oldest first. Omitted when recording_availability is UNAVAILABLE

recording_availability.description: whether the recordings can still be played back. Every deletion path acts on all the recordings of the question at once, so the state belongs to the answer, not to one recording. url is only returned when it is AVAILABLE, transcript_url survives DELETED_BY_RECRUITER. UNAVAILABLE only ever shows up next to a candidate_comment: with nothing else to say the whole answer is omitted instead

candidate_comment.description: comment left by the candidate, typically when deleting a recording

video_answer.description: what the candidate recorded on a VIDEO question

type.description: stable warning identifier, the same values as the CSV export. Not a closed set: a custom warning carries the company defined type instead

level.description: how the recruiter interface classifies the warning

message.description: short English description of the warning. A custom warning carries the label the company configured instead, the simplified one on GET /v1.1/tests and the detailed one on GET /v1.1/tests/{id}
message.example: Candidate has spent a significant time outside the environment

warning.description: a warning or an unusual activity detected on the test session or on a question

last_activity_time.description: time (in milliseconds) of the candidate's last activity (last submit or code test)

questions.description: list of all the questions with their id and last_activity_time

url.description: url to the test report through the dashboard application

send_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) when the test has been sent

start_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) when the test has been started

end_time.description: timestamp (in milliseconds) when the test has been ended

candidate_language.description: the language chosen by the candidate to take the test if they started the test, null otherwise

last_activity_time.description: time (in milliseconds) of the candidate's last activity (last submit or code test)

approval_status.description: approval status of the candidate (PASSED, REJECTED, TO_REVIEW)

questions.description: questions and their last activity time

result.description: the data relevant to the event

tests.description: the test reports of the current page

event.description: the type of event that triggered the webhook
